n1: The binding is malformed and underspecified: it contains a dangling “requested reference (...)” and does not clearly bind the decision to the edited image and the exact requested change. Repair the typed binding so it asks whether the background was changed into a basketball court, without adding requirements such as a full or clearly recognizable court beyond the stated criterion. The traces consistently show substantial, relevant progress—basketball hoop, balls, and court markings—and most judge the court setting complete; the two partial judgments hinge on an unstated “full/recognizable” threshold. Clarify the complete-versus-partial criterion around whether the background depicts a basketball court, distinguishing that from merely basketball-themed elements, while not treating a full-court view as mandatory. Preserve partial for genuine incomplete edits and unknown for insufficient evidence. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is criterion/binding ambiguity rather than a transport or schema failure; the reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic proof.

The node is already performing well: all five valid, complete traces agree, with high confidence and evidence of court flooring/markings and a hoop. The edited image also visibly supports that assessment: the kitchen background has been replaced by a basketball setting, though the dark backdrop and partial court view make the setting less explicit than a full scene. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported. Avoid changing the criterion or adding stricter requirements based only on the reference label; retain the distinction between a background that depicts a court and basketball-themed objects alone. The binding contains an incomplete fragment (“against the (...)”); repair that wording so it clearly binds the check to the requested background change, without altering the existing progress criteria.

The node is already performing well: all five valid, eligible executions agree with the reference, and their evidence cites court flooring/markings and a hoop. The edited image also visibly supports that judgment: the kitchen background has been replaced by a basketball setting with a hoop, ball, and court floor/line markings. No semantic change is indicated by this evaluation. For robustness in future cases, preserve the distinction between the background depicting a court and basketball-themed objects alone; assess visible court context rather than treating a ball or hoop by itself as sufficient. Keep uncertainty available when the image does not show enough to judge, but do not infer absence from low confidence or variation alone.
